plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: it guarantees winning whenever the value exceeds the second-highest bid (positive profit) and avoids overpaying since the price paid is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Given my value of $25, the optimal action is to bid exactly $25, ensuring truthful revelation and maximizing expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. I will bid my true value of $31.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and independent private values uniformly distributed on $0-$49. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $9, so I should bid exactly $9 to ensure optimal outcomes.
